questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose McGill because I heard good things about the university, it's academic level and progressiveness within fields of my interest. Also, Montreal seemed like a good city to live and study in, neither too expensive nor too big but still a city with a lot going on.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The first half of the semester with a strict covid lockdown and a very cold winter was pretty rough, which is why I chose 7.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found all the immigration stuff a bit confusing to be honest. But I think it was very related to having the exchange semester postponed/cancelled several times and everything related to covid-19 travel restrictions. However, McGill were generally fairly easy to reach and had some informative webinars with the essential information so everything worked out fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because of covid all our new/exchange/international students activities were held online, but I think it would be different usually. Also received e-mails with information about the most important stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Taken the circumstances into account it was pretty good. I found it easy to get in contact with the students service at McGill whether by e-mail, phone or google teams appointments.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Montreal is a really good city in this aspect. It is fairly easy to find housing and not super expensive (around 400-800 dollars per month). I can recommend living off-campus, most of what I heard about living on campus is that it is expensive, not very high standard and that most people there are very young. There are some good facebook groups for housing I think one is called "McGill off-campus housing", if you have time to arrive before the semester starts I think it is easiest to find something once you're in the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great, you get to see more of the city than just the Downtown/McGill area which is not necessarily the most interesting. The areas plateau/mile end/outremont are really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Once you get it, it is fine, but do set aside some time to figure it out.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email mcgill if you have any issues, or email the specific instructors/professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was only one out of the 4 courses I hoped for that I never managed to get, which I think is fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress, it seems a bit confusing at first but really is not. Write an email to the professor if you need specific prerequisites or if you have trouble registering for their course. Check minerva very often if there is a course you really want. In the meantime just register for some that you wouldn't mind taking. Remember to read about the courses on minerva as well, sometimes there is some additional information available which is not written in the course catalogue.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a really good time with most of my classes, inspiring, engaging professors and great texts.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three 400-level and one 300-level which was a good combination. Would say the 400 level were my own level, but since the workload is higher at McGill it was really nice to have one "easy" class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more work during a week. Approx. same amount of reading for each course, but the number of small papers/assignments, mid terms, presentations etc. was much higher. However, I didn't find the professors to expect particularly advanced work, seemed they mostly wanted to "check" that people actually read and understood.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CANS 306: Issues in Native Studies
CANS 405: Cdn Studies Seminar 5 - Black-Indigenous Politics: From Recognition to Solidarity and Decolonization
ENG 444: Studies Women's Writing & Feminist Theory - Gender and African Literature
GFSF 406: Trans*Feminisms

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I especially liked the Trans*Feminisms course, which was taught by Calev Litvack who is an amazing and engaging professor! I really enjoyed ENG 444 as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The health insurance at McGill is a bit expensive, and you can actually get a RamQ card for free instead! Look it up.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are expensive generally. PA and Seagal are much better than Metro and Provigo though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think generally they are fine, but because of covid not much was happening except for a few online activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again, I don't know much about it, but think there are several clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend joining the McGill outdoor club they have a cool house and also try and look up the ski club if you like skiing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Quebec city, Toronto, New York, go skiing in Quebec or in the north of US, go hiking in the national parks, take trips to the coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, I think the university culture is quite similar, maybe only people are a bit younger in general.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in class. Generally I didn't find a lot of people at McGill are actually from Montreal, but other places in Canada or US or international, so try and seek out other environments as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hm, I think compared to Danes, people here are less reserved but maybe more difficult to really get to know.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of cool events and cultural activities going on Montreal, which were easy to find and access.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Everything seems a bit confusing from home/at first, but don't worry it will be fine 2) Try to meet people through other places than just uni, seek out your interests/hobbies/communities in the city 3) Live off-campus maybe in a shared flat, it is a good way to meet (local) people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look for courses outside your own department, as an Anthropology student I could take courses in the whole Arts faculty (both social sciences and humanities) which was a really cool opportunity.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Really good courses and inspiring professors, meeting new people and enjoying the music/art/film/party scenes of Montreal.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably covid.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
